topic.title: Pre-PEP: UTF-8 String Representation
topic.text:
I am considering using UTF-8 as Unicode’s internal representation. The potential benefits are:

PEP 393’s Flexible String Representation (FSR) is an implementation detail and is not part of the Stable ABI. Some extension modules use the fastest available APIs for performance reasons, which makes moving to the Stable ABI harder. Eliminating the overhead of creating a UTF-8 cache could help encourage Stable ABI adoption.

Python is a glue language. C, C++, and Rust have many libraries that process UTF-8 efficiently, but supporting FSR requires hand-written code.

UTF-8 can use less memory for large strings when only some characters require the 4-byte kind.

Reference implementation

Specification

Ordinary non-ASCII strings retain a UTF-8 representation. The PEP 393 fixed-width representation (FSR) is created and retained only when needed.

Lone surrogates are preserved internally using surrogatepass , without changing Python-level semantics such as string length and indexing.

Strings under construction with PyUnicode_New() continue to use a writable FSR.

Many paths, including string operations, UnicodeWriter , codecs, and JSON, have been changed to process UTF-8 directly or read characters sequentially.

PyUnicode_KIND() returns the width of the fixed-width representation. PyUnicode_DATA() and the various *_DATA() functions create the FSR lazily, so they may return NULL if memory is exhausted.
